_meta.description: What the filing does not tell us. Absence of disclosure is not evidence of weakness.

items.title: Revenue by product (API vs Claude Code vs Cowork vs Claude.ai)
items.status: Not disclosed. Only consumption (79%) vs subscription (21%) and the Claude Code spend-intensity comparison.
items.whyItMatters: Determines whether Anthropic is an API utility or an application company — and how exposed it is to routing layers like Copilot Fusion.
items.whatWeCanBound: Consumption revenue is 'primarily generated from customers building applications incorporating Claude or utilizing our first-party applications' — the two are mixed.
items.disclosureNeeded: Product-line revenue or Claude Code users/ARR.

items.title: Model-by-model profitability
items.whyItMatters: Mythos/Fable list at 2.5× Opus; margins by class drive the mix risk as customers route to cheaper models.
items.disclosureNeeded: Gross margin by model class or price realization.

items.title: Training vs inference compute
items.status: Not disclosed. Functional split gives cost of revenue $4.8B vs R&D $19.2B (9M 2026).
items.whyItMatters: Separates the cost of serving (falling) from the cost of staying at the frontier (rising).
items.whatWeCanBound: Upper bound: ≤25.6% of compute expense is customer-serving (cost of revenue ÷ compute).
items.disclosureNeeded: Compute by workload (research, training, serving, internal use).

items.title: True accelerator utilization
items.whyItMatters: Idle committed capacity is the core downside of a $895B commitment stack.
items.whatWeCanBound: Q3 short-term buying suggests high utilization of committed capacity in Q3.
items.disclosureNeeded: Utilization or capacity (GW) online vs committed.

items.title: Gross retention and mature-cohort expansion
items.whyItMatters: Separates durable expansion from churned experiments.
items.whatWeCanBound: None — NRR is dollar-weighted and nets churn.
items.disclosureNeeded: Gross dollar retention; NRR for customers ≥$100K at base.

items.title: Identity and share of top customers
items.status: Customers are anonymized (A–E). Top five ≈25% of 9M revenue; no customer ≥10%.
items.whyItMatters: AI-native platforms embedding Claude can switch providers quickly.
items.whatWeCanBound: Customer C was 43% of 2023 revenue and 11% of H1 2026.
items.disclosureNeeded: Named customers above 10% or by category (AI-native vs enterprise).

items.title: Revenue by industry and by function
items.whyItMatters: Tests whether adoption is spreading beyond software.
items.whatWeCanBound: Case studies span finance, retail, pharma, telecom, insurance.

items.title: Direct vs marketplace economics (fee rates by CSP)
items.status: Partially disclosed: marketplace share 44% (9M); channel fees +$4.8B; terms changed.
items.whyItMatters: Determines how much of each Anthropic dollar hyperscalers capture.
items.whatWeCanBound: Channel fees ≈14% of total revenue; take rate on marketplace revenue cannot be isolated because fees may apply beyond marketplace billing.
items.disclosureNeeded: Fee rates or channel revenue by CSP.

items.title: Fully loaded cost per agentic task
items.status: Not disclosed; only relative claims (−40% Opus 5.5, −25% Fable 5.1).
items.whyItMatters: The real unit of competition for agents.
items.disclosureNeeded: Absolute cost per task for reference workloads.

items.title: October 31 Run-Rate Revenue
items.whyItMatters: The only post-Q3 operating datapoint promised by the document.

items.title: Nature and geography of policy-violating revenue
items.whyItMatters: Indicates whether the leakage is distillation, resale, sanctioned access or fraud — each with different competitive implications.
items.whatWeCanBound: Distillation, geo-restrictions and fraud are discussed separately in risk factors.
items.disclosureNeeded: Breakdown by violation category and region.

items.title: Revenue by country / APAC / Japan
items.status: Only US vs international by billing address (70.6% / 29.4%).
items.whyItMatters: Billing address understates international usage via US-billed multinationals and CSP marketplaces.
items.whatWeCanBound: International share rose from 26.7% (FY2025) to 29.4% (9M 2026); APAC/Japan not separated.
